q-45293.name: Question 1
q-45293.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $b.$ To do this, we first cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4kb}{3} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ 4\cdot 4kb & =3\cdot 3 \\ 16kb & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $16k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}16kb & =9 \\ \frac{16kb}{16k} & =\frac{9}{16k} \\ \frac{\cancel{16k}b}{\cancel{16k}} & =\frac{9}{16k} \\ b & =\frac{9}{16k}\end{aligned}
$$

q-45320.name: Question 2
q-45320.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $5$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}2lx & =\frac{6}{5} \\ 5\cdot 2lx & =5\cdot \frac{6}{5} \\ 10lx & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to isolate $x.$ To do this, we divide both sides of the equation by $10l:$

$$
\begin{aligned}10lx & =6 \\ \frac{10lx}{10l} & =\frac{6}{10l} \\ \frac{\cancel{10l}x}{\cancel{10l}} & =\frac{6}{10l} \\ x & =\frac{6}{10l}\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2\cdot 3}{2\cdot 5l} \\ x & =\frac{\cancel{2}\cdot 3}{\cancel{2}\cdot 5l} \\ x & =\frac{3}{5l}\end{aligned}
$$

If 2lx=65, then x=

a
53l
b
3−5l
c
3+5l
d
−23l
e
35l
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we multiply both sides of the equation by 5 to get rid of the fraction:

2lx=655⋅2lx=5⋅6510lx=6

Now, we need to isolate x. To do this, we divide both sides of the equation by 10l:

10lx=610lx10l=610l10lx10l=610lx=610l

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows:

x=2⋅32⋅5lx=2⋅32⋅5lx=35l

q-45326.name: Question 3
q-45326.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $g.$ To do this, we first cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5mg}{8} & =\frac{5}{2} \\ 2\cdot 5mg & =8\cdot 5 \\ 10mg & =40\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $10m:$

$$
\begin{aligned}10mg & =40 \\ \frac{10mg}{10m} & =\frac{40}{10m} \\ \frac{\cancel{10m}g}{\cancel{10m}} & =\frac{40}{10m} \\ g & =\frac{40}{10m}\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}g & =\frac{10\cdot 4}{10m} \\ g & =\frac{\cancel{10}\cdot 4}{\cancel{10}m} \\ g & =\frac{4}{m}\end{aligned}
$$
